independence: Different stateless turn/agent ID than candidate author; no candidate code or checkpoint modified.
limitations: Exact symbolic controls contain the binary addition law; they are not learned, trained, or parameter-matched with RLT.
Dense 16-state matrix control is not a benchmark of a full dense Transformer; compare kernels only, no generalized architectural efficiency claim.
Only 128 8-bit tasks; not 16/32-bit transfer, not a statistical power/performance claim.
Repeated timing trials on one host can be affected by system load/cache/turbo and are not independent learning seeds.
CUDA disabled but no OS-enforced CPU isolation or calibrated power meter.
No new neural model trained; training energy, training time, and training data cost not measured.
GPU disabled through environment only; no OS-enforced process isolation.
Separate agent ID does not authenticate a distinct real-world human.
Original time results are not bitwise reproducible under differing system load.
next_action: Later independent task owner/finalizer may run dag.py pass with this evidence; current verifier must not self-finalize.
proof_scope: Independent pinned-source and checkpoint hash audit; 5 benchmark arms x 3 fresh-process trials on the same 128 unique 8-bit unsigned modular-addition pairs, repeated five times per process (640 verified results/trial/arm); 3 fixed symbolic controls exhaustively evaluated over all 65,536 pairs; corruption and altered-summary negatives detected. One host and one seed11 checkpoint per neural arm; no training or energy instrumentation. Timing is host-load and software dependent and does not prove general architecture superiority or extrapolate to other arithmetic tasks.
